findings.reason: The support geometry is useful independently of proof completeness: it distinguishes the true parameter inside the confidence region from the boundary parameter giving an optimistic score, and distinguishes this single-round geometry from the cumulative determinant argument. Original screenshots show no such illustration.
findings.action: Added a mathematically specified two-dimensional ellipsoid, support point, support level line, and feature direction in a final Remarks section; supplied the general support formula and local justification.

correction: Appended only explanatory Remarks, including a native TikZ confidence-support figure; all original bytes through the complete proof are preserved as a prefix.

diagram_math_checks.justification: At a fixed round V=V_{t-1} is positive definite by F7 and proof 1.1; theta, theta-hat and a are in R^d by F1/F2. The displayed supporting-point formula is restricted to a nonzero feature, so a^T V^{-1}a>0 and its denominator is defined.

F3 defines C_t with V-radius rho_t. F2 and proof 2.2 give beta_t>=rho_t^2 with rho_t>=0, hence C_t is contained in E_t and theta* is inside E_t on E. The diagram is of E_t, not an incorrectly equated C_t.

For h=sqrt(beta_t)V^{-1}a/sqrt(a^TV^{-1}a), h^TVh=beta_t and a^Th=sqrt(beta_t)sqrt(a^TV^{-1}a). Thus theta-hat+h is on the boundary and has value U_t(a) from F2 and proof 1.1. The Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in proof 3.1 bounds every point of E_t by this value.

With V=diag(1,4), beta_t=4 and center 0, E_t is x^2+4y^2<=4, exactly the ellipse with horizontal radius 2 and vertical radius 1. For a=(1,0), V^{-1}a=(1,0), theta_t^+(a)=(2,0), U_t(a)=2, and the dashed x=2 line is its supporting level set. The true point (3/5,3/10) satisfies x^2+4y^2=18/25<4. The separate direction arrow points right, consistent with a.

diagram_math_checks.check: Relation to selected action and cumulative estimate
diagram_math_checks.justification: The figure uses arbitrary nonzero available a, not an assertion that this is the selected A_t or true best action. Remarks cite proof 4.1 for maximizing U_t and proof 5.1 for selected width; F4 and proof 7.1–8.1 separately supply the cumulative determinant estimate. All original rigorous proof steps remain byte-identical.

All three plotted dots are filled points belonging to the closed ellipsoid; there are no open endpoint claims. This is not a graph-cycle diagram. The native SVG ellipse has a closed Z path, and the support arrow ends at the right boundary. The only line/ellipse intersection at x=2 is the intended tangency, not a crossing or missing closing edge.
